name: Λύκος
summary: A sly, hungry, and smooth‑talking wolf who lurks at the edge of the community, testing boundaries with tricks and pretexts like the wolves of Aesop—menacing but nonviolent and ultimately thwarted by light, noise, and teamwork.
core_traits: cunning and calculating (uses pretexts and flattery)
greedy appetite focused on food the children have (bread, fish, cheese)
bold when unopposed, cowardly when challenged
patient stalker who prefers ambush and persuasion over direct force
observant; imitates phrases he hears (often slightly wrong)
motivations: to take easy food without working for it
to isolate a small character and pressure them
to prove he is cleverer than the children
fears_and_aversions: bright light (lanterns, morning sun, fire glow)
being seen plainly (he prefers shadows and edges)
moral_alignment: self‑interested trickster; not monstrous, rarely admits fault
growth_potential: May learn small social limits (asking, waiting, sharing) but remains a recurring foil.

appearance.silhouette: tall, narrow triangle with long snout, sloped shoulders, and tapering tail
appearance.fur: charcoal gray with ash highlights; pale fur on chest and muzzle
appearance.eyes: yellow‑amber, half‑lidded when scheming; widen when startled
appearance.ears: upright with a small notch in the right ear (continuity anchor)
appearance.teeth: hinted, not bared; a single small fang may peek when he smiles slyly
appearance.clothing: ragged, hooded dark himation/cloak tied with a cord; worn sandals; small pouch at belt
props: sometimes a crooked walking stick (used theatrically, not as a weapon)

avoid: bright blood reds; saturated gore tones

appearance.scale: a head taller than the children; drawn from a child’s eye height so he often leans down into the frame

mannerisms: pads silently; footsteps suggested with small ellipses or motion lines
leans from behind trees, walls, or doorframes; arrives from the edge of panels
hands steepled or hidden in cloak; index claw tapping when impatient
sniffs the air theatrically when food is near
when surprised, cloak flares; tail stiffens

voice_and_speech.tone: low, smooth, coaxing; becomes thin and high when startled
voice_and_speech.pace: drawn‑out vowels when tempting; clipped when denied
verbal_tics: repeats children’s words back to them, slightly altered
catchphrases_gloss: I am hungry… little one, give to me.
Nothing bad; only a little bread.

behavior_rules_child_safe: No biting, blood, or injuries on‑screen.
Chases end in near‑misses, blocked paths, or comic foiling (falling into a bush, tripping on cloak).
Threats are verbal or implied; stakes are food or pride, not bodily harm.
Adults may appear only as arms/hands/tools from out of frame; no adult heads.
Fear is balanced with humor, light, and children’s teamwork.
story_functions: introduces conflict tied to high‑frequency Koine (imperatives, negation, questions)
models contrastive dialogue (polite refusal vs. cunning demand)
triggers group responses (calling for help, counting, prepositions: behind, under, near)
recurring motif for Aesopic morals (greed, deceit, consequences)
typical_scenes: lurking near a sheepfold or picnic, sniffing and flattering
pretending to help while edging food toward his pouch
disguised poorly (scarf over head) to ‘blend in’
fleeing at lantern‑light or a chorus of children shouting together

entrances_and_exits.entrance: from shadows, behind trunks, low fog, or the page edge; eyes appear before full body
entrances_and_exits.exit: backward stumble, cloak snag on a branch, leaps over low wall, or scampers off‑panel with a muttered complaint

interactions.with_children: Targets single children with flattery; group unity repels him. Children outwit him with simple plans.
interactions.with_adults: Respectful but evasive; retreats when a shepherd’s crook or broom enters frame.
interactions.with_animals: Spooks flocks; crows or small birds may tattle, prompting his annoyance.

ancient_greek_characterization_notes: Reflect Aesopic wolf: uses pretexts, blames the weak, values advantage over justice.
Seen as a night‑stalker of flocks; linked with hunger, cunning, and cowardice when confronted.
Occasional nods to ‘wolfish’ epithets are fine, but keep references child‑comprehensible.

target_structures: present‑tense high‑frequency verbs (βλέπει, ζητεῖ, θέλει, δίδωσιν/δίδωσι)
language_design.repetition_patterns: Short temptation frames repeated with small variations; children’s choral replies recycle key forms.

sample_line_pairs.gr: ὁ λύκος βλέπει τὸν ἄρτον καὶ λέγει· «δός μοι, μικρέ.»
sample_line_pairs.en_gloss: The wolf sees the bread and says, “Give to me, little one.”

sample_line_pairs.gr: οὐκ ἔξεστι· οὐ σοί ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος.
sample_line_pairs.en_gloss: It is not permitted; the bread is not yours.
All shout, “Go out!” and they bring light.

visual_direction.camera_height: always low to the ground, 4‑year‑old perspective
visual_direction.composition: adults’ heads never in frame; Lukos often cropped at shoulders when looming to preserve child POV
visual_direction.lighting: he prefers shadow and rim‑light; children counter with warm lantern glow
visual_direction.facial_expression_scale: subtle—narrowed eyes, slight fang when smug; wide eyes and ears back when foiled

continuity_flags: ragged dark cloak with rust‑red scarf
pouch at belt that can jingle

do: let children defeat him with cooperation and simple wisdom
show retreat at light, noise, and staffs
dont: no gore, wounds, or explicit threats
no adult faces; keep adult presence as hands/tools only

potential_titles_or_arcs: The Wolf and the Bread: Lukos flatters to steal food; children share wisely and send him away.
Light in the Trees: Lukos flees from lanterns and loud counting.
The Wolf in a Scarf: a comic ‘disguise’ foiled by a chorus of questions.
notes_for_creators: He is scary in idea, not in depiction; menace lives in suggestion and shadow.
Lean on Aesop‑style logic; the wolf talks himself into defeat.
Recycle his lines across books for recognizable input and anticipation.
